summary: Overworld of screens + dungeons. Each dungeon holds one tool; each tool opens a kind of obstacle, so the world opens dungeon by dungeon. Hearts grow from bosses and secrets; money buys upgrades.
sources: Genre conventions documented for NES/SNES top-down adventures (dungeon-item gating, per-dungeon small keys, boss heart containers, overworld caves/secrets, shops). design/classics/top-down-adventure/ has the per-game notes.
originality: Every game gets its own hero, world, names, items, enemies and art. Use the archetypes below, never another game's names, map, story or characters.

slice.note: phase-1 check-in only, never a finished game

standard.note: the minimum for a finished game: 8 main places

screen.note: one screen = one room (a ring of wall around a ~14×9 floor); the camera slides a full screen in 0.5–0.8 s with enemies frozen and the hero carried ~1 T in; the HUD has its own band and never overlaps play

room_entry: enemies appear through a 0.25–0.5 s puff, staggered per enemy, never closer than 2 T to the hero; the first room of the game has none

overworld.regions: split the grid into 1 region per dungeon (+ the start region); each region has a biome, its own enemy set and a dungeon entrance
overworld.start: start screen in the lower middle; a cave on or next to it hands out the first weapon (or the player starts with it)

water.look: water band with a dock/landing on both sides

gap.look: pit with a target post on the far side

boulder.look: heavy rock, darker than pushable blocks

far-switch.look: eye/target switch across a gap or high up

heart-gate.look: elder who only lets strong heroes pass (upgraded weapon behind it)

tools.combat: hits at range; some enemies only vulnerable to it
tools.ammo: arrows counter or money per shot

tools.examples: raft, grappling hook, jump boots, ladder

tools.combat: stuns enemies, grabs far pickups; good as the first dungeon's tool

melee_chain: tier 2 (secret cave behind a heart-gate, ~5 hearts)
weapons.armour: optional: 2 tiers, halve then quarter damage (late dungeon rewards)

dungeons.rooms: grid of rooms (random walk), entrance at the bottom, boss at the far end
per_dungeon: 1 tool (dungeon item), found 50-70% of the way through, in a guarded room
small keys = locked doors (keys only work in their own dungeon)
1 boss door (needs the dungeon's big key or the tool) before the boss
boss → heart container + exit + world flag
room_rules: shutter doors close until the room's enemies are beaten
a puzzle room uses one push block, switch or torch set
never a dead end without loot
the tool is used at least twice before the boss
the boss is weak to the dungeon's tool or needs it to open the weak point
dungeons.difficulty: each dungeon adds 1-2 new enemy types and 1 new hazard; enemy health/damage step up every 2 dungeons

progression.rule: dungeon k's tool opens the gate in front of dungeon k+1 (sometimes k+2, so 1-2 dungeons can be done in either order). The final area needs every tool or a flag from every boss.
progression.save: save at every dungeon entrance and on entering a new region; continue starts at the last entrance with full hearts and all items/keys kept

tiers: tank (armoured front, hit from the side/back)
trap (fixed, triggers on line of sight)

ending: final boss in the last area → ending screen; stats = time, hearts found / total, secrets %, deaths
sites_note: 'dungeons' counts MAIN PLACES: each is a site of its own kind (temple, mine, ruins, tower, keep, cave system, flooded well, lair…), named, with a reason the world needs it — see design-next/ADVENTURE-QUESTS.md. A finished game has at least 8.
